headline: Deep learning and benchmarks test omics models for generalization across populations
label: Omics Deep Learning Benchmarks
summary: Recent benchmarks and architectures probe whether pretrained and graph-based omics models generalize across populations, modalities, and sample regimes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is testing whether learned omics representations hold up beyond their training conditions. EHI benchmarks 1,475 multi-population deep learning tasks for cancer prognosis and quantifies performance disparities across populations, and an instruction-tuned tabular foundation model with in-context learning is reported to reduce ancestry-group gaps in genomic risk prediction. HADACA3 runs over 250,000 pipelines and finds multi-omics integration does not beat DNAm alone for deconvolution. Method papers adapt architectures to specific tasks: PEARL applies spectral graph convolution to multi-omics classification, GEDI 2.0 reimplements a single-cell generative model with a C++ core, and mmContext applies contrastive learning to omics and text embeddings. What is new is equity-oriented evaluation paired with architectural adaptation and direct tests of whether multi-omics integration adds value.
